key_insight: The paper presents a modular pipeline that generates longitudinal synthetic clinical notes with large language models while aiming to preserve internal consistency across a patient’s full hospital journey.
clinical_relevance: It offers privacy-preserving synthetic documentation that can help develop and evaluate clinical AI tools such as summarization, coding, and decision-support systems without using real patient records.
method: Generate structured synthetic patients first, then simulate semi-structured care journeys.
Use LLMs to produce unstructured clinical notes with varied style, structure, and detail.
Add LLM-based validation and augmentation to improve realism, faithfulness, and diversity.
evidence_signal: The release includes 70 synthetic patients with 20–50 notes each, and the dataset is provided at multiple validation levels to trade off realism against scalability.
watch_item: Synthetic notes may still contain inconsistencies or artifacts despite validation, so fit-for-purpose checking is needed before using them for downstream model development.
paper_title: A Pipeline for Generating Longitudinal Synthetic Clinical Notes Using Large Language Models
